_comment: 🛑 DO NOT APPLY THIS FILE YET. 🛑
S3 bucket policy ADDITION — shramsafal-uploads-prod. Encryption-header deny.
spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN §11 (S11-infra-author)
Split out of bucket-policy.json per round-1 review finding C1 (2026-08-15).
Authored because it is a reasonable defence-in-depth goal, NOT presented as
safe to apply — same posture as
aws/raw/bucket-policy-cmk-deny-rail.PHASE2-DO-NOT-APPLY.json.
WHY THIS IS NOT SAFE TO APPLY TODAY, STATED PLAINLY:
A Deny with Null:{s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption:true} on s3:PutObject
checks the REQUEST HEADER, not the bucket's default encryption — the two
are unrelated. Default encryption fills in AFTER the object is accepted;
this condition fires BEFORE that, on the request itself. So applying this
denies every write that omits the header, independent of whether default
encryption would have covered it.
TWO CONCRETE HAZARDS, NEITHER RULED OUT BY ANYTHING IN THIS REPO:
1. UNAUDITED WRITER. No in-repo pipeline is confirmed to write
_deploy/, _deploys/, deploys/, or apk/ on this bucket (grep across
.github/, aws/, scripts/ for s3 cp / s3 sync targeting
shramsafal-uploads-prod: no matches; android-release.yml writes
shramsafal-app-prod instead, a different bucket). ~618 MB of deploy
artifacts are written by something outside this repo's visibility.
Plain `aws s3 cp` sends no SSE header unless --sse is explicitly
passed. Whether the actual writer passes it cannot be determined from
source — this needs either (a) locating and reading the actual deploy
tooling (likely on the EC2 host or in the private _COFOUNDER/ tree,
out of this lane's scope), or (b) a CloudTrail data-event query over a
representative window showing 100% of PutObject calls to this bucket
already carry the header.
2. MULTIPART. s3:PutObject Deny with a Null SSE condition also covers
UploadPart (multipart parts share the s3:PutObject IAM action).
UploadPart requests structurally CANNOT carry
x-amz-server-side-encryption — it is set once, at
CreateMultipartUpload, not per part. Any object crossing the
multipart threshold (default 8 MB via the aws s3 high-level CLI;
_deploy/ holds 44 MB tarballs) would be denied on every part upload
even when the initiator set the header correctly at initiation. This
would need testing against this bucket's actual multipart threshold
and initiator behaviour before it is safe.
TO MAKE THIS SAFE TO APPLY:
Verify (1) via CloudTrail data events or by reading the actual deploy
pipeline that writes _deploy/ / _deploys/ / deploys/ / apk/, AND verify
(2) by confirming either that nothing here ever multiparts, or by adding
an explicit multipart-safe carve-out (e.g. scoping the Deny to only the
prefixes with a confirmed compliant writer, or dropping the Null check in
favour of a StringNotEquals that only fires on PutObject, not
UploadPart — StringNotEquals with Null-header still has the same gap, so
this needs a genuinely different condition shape, not just a substitution).
Once verified, merge this Statement into bucket-policy.json's Statement
array (do not apply as a second separate put-bucket-policy call — that
replaces the whole policy document and would drop the TLS-only
statement) and apply via aws/uploads/apply-config.sh as one transaction.
